# (the whole repository)

Compiled from `contracts/rules`. Change a rule there (`npm run learn -- ...`), never here.

- **invariant** `root/emit-clean-commented-code-person-can`: Emit clean, commented code that a person can edit. Prefer the simple obvious form over the clever one; rich-but-commented CSS is the house style.
- **invariant** `root/green-gate-human-seeing-work-observable`: A green gate is not a human seeing it. Work that is observable in the product adds its OWN FILE under `docs/acceptance/owner-queue/` in the same commit: what changed, the ROUTE to it in under a minute, what to look at, and the date. One file per item, never a shared list. An item with no route is not an item.
- **invariant** `root/keep-generated-template-self-contained-runtime`: Keep a generated template self-contained: no runtime dependencies and no CDN references, relative paths only in exports. GSAP and the Lottie player are bundled locally and the player is injected only when a template uses a Lottie asset.
- **invariant** `root/land-through-run-session-owns-branch`: Land through `/queue-merge`, run in the session that owns the branch when that work is FINISHED. Queueing IS the declaration that the work is done and only that session can make it, so nobody else queues your branch. Never merge into `main` yourself and never drive `safe-merge` by hand.
- **invariant** `root/lesson-recorded-rule-goes-evidence-compiled`: A lesson is recorded with `npm run learn`: the rule goes to `contracts/rules/`, the evidence to `contracts/records/`, and the compiled `.claude/rules/` files are never edited by hand.
- **invariant** `root/never-occupy-checkout-holds-feature-branch`: Never occupy the checkout that holds `main` with a feature branch, and never read or build there. A build there gates `main` instead of your branch while still reporting green; the build stamp is what says which.
- **invariant** `root/publishing-past-still-needs-user-message`: Publishing PAST `main` still needs the user, in that message - publishing a package, anything costing money. Those are not landings, because a later commit cannot take them back.
- **invariant** `root/question-owner-names-reason-own-text`: A question to the owner names its reason in its own text - `needs: account`, `money`, `identity`, `harness` or `alignment` - or it is not his. A merge conflict, a design choice, which option, when: consult the strongest model available, decide, record it where he can revert it, and keep working.
- **invariant** `root/treat-code-single-source-truth-canonical`: Treat the CODE as the single source of truth. `SpxTemplate` is canonical, and every visual, AI or block action emits a deterministic readable code patch - never a hidden scene model - so the editor always reflects exactly what was written.
- **invariant** `root/validate-before-export-block-export-errors`: Validate before export and block export on errors. The platform owns SPX compatibility, never the AI.
- **invariant** `root/version-every-persisted-format-ship-breaking`: Version every persisted format, and ship a breaking change together with its migration in the same commit. Additive optional fields never bump the version; a breaking change bumps it and migrates ON READ so everything downstream sees one shape; serialization always writes the current version; an unknown version degrades to read-only rather than crashing.
- **invariant** `root/write-blocks-deterministic-transforms-template-template`: Write blocks and AI as deterministic transforms from template to template that insert clean code.
- **invariant** `wizard/derive-what-counts-graphic-type-setup`: DERIVE what counts as a graphic type setup value, never declare it twice: `setupFields` drops every field an operator event carries as its PAYLOAD, because in this model a pick IS payload, and image fields stay out because their value is an asset path. A design with none shows no section at all.
- **invariant** `wizard/keep-finish-wizard-branch-carrying-graphic`: Keep Finish the wizard ONE branch, carrying the graphic name from `draft.name` applied inside `buildDraftTemplate` so it reaches the topbar, the Save prefill and the export slug through one path. Blank falls back to the design catalog name. That name slugs the zip and, for the SPX and CasparCG targets, the template FOLDER inside it.
- **invariant** `wizard/keep-three-deliberate-divergences-rest-wizard`: Keep three deliberate divergences from the rest of the wizard on the Entry step: no kit card, cards act on CLICK rather than radio-plus-Continue, and Blank stays behind Advanced mode. `e2e/wizard-entry-fit.spec.ts` pins them.
- **invariant** `wizard/offer-pro-tier-only-where-can`: Offer the Pro tier only where it can actually run - the status answer AND the metering backend - and where that is false make it ABSENT, never a greyed row and never a key request. Its settings are one read-back with the remaining allowance and no chooser of any kind: no provider, no model, no key. A hosted deployment is never reachable from the browser through a flag, a query parameter or a stored key.
- **invariant** `wizard/say-user-own-coding-agent-route`: Say the user OWN CODING AGENT route before any tier and any key: one visible line under the section head, the install lines and the docs link behind a "show me" that opens exactly when the settings sheet opens itself, a pointer FIRST in that sheet, and a clause on the bring-your-own-key hint. It is copy and a link, never a tier - nothing runs there. Take the commands from the distribution table, never invent them.
- **invariant** `wizard/say-which-layers-travel-never-how`: Say WHICH layers travel, never how each one behaves: there is no per-row move-or-grow picker, every listed layer moves, and furniture drawn to the growing panel own two edges stretches by itself without ever being a row. The mode survives in the draft and in the saved layout for a pro editing the code, never as a control. A text layer past the edge is ARTWORK: state it in one line and commit it WITH the set.
- **invariant** `wizard/start-every-detected-text-row-prefix`: Start EVERY detected text row ON. The `f:` prefix guarantees a field and never turns an unmarked row off; only a PICTURE is off by default and switched on by it. The step has a measured HEIGHT BUDGET pinned exactly by the fold cases: a copy change costing a checklist row fails, and one buying a row updates the number.
- **trap** `landing/generated-file-merges-cleanly-still-comes`: A generated file merges cleanly and still comes out wrong. When a branch and main both regenerate the same compiled artefact, git resolves the two texts without a conflict and can drop whole regions of either side. After taking main in, re-run the generator and commit whatever it changes; never trust the merged text of a file a script writes.
- **trap** `root/enqueue-browser-driving-work-rather-than`: ENQUEUE browser-driving work with `npm run queue` rather than waiting for a slot, because one such job runs per MACHINE and this laptop is RAM-bound. A suite, a catalog sweep, a bench and a spike are the same workload. Name a new browser-driving script like its siblings so `SWEEP_SCRIPTS` sees it, or add it there.
- **trap** `root/keep-boot-watchdog-connection-check-working`: Keep the `/app` boot watchdog and connection check working: `?diag=1` renders the inline diagnostics with main.tsx standing down, durable-store hydration times out to localStorage, and a boot that never mounts paints a plain-HTML diagnosis.
- **trap** `root/read-build-own-exit-code-never`: Read a build's own exit code, never a pipeline's: `npm run build > log 2>&1; echo $?`, because piping the build through `tail` or `head` reports the pipe's status and a failing gate reads as green.
- **trap** `root/read-which-jobs-ran-before-believing`: Read WHICH JOBS RAN before believing a green run, and re-run an unchanged sha before bisecting a job that stopped at its own `timeout-minutes`. A stop at the cap is not a verdict, and a green run is not one either until you have read the job list.
- **trap** `templates/after-graphic-settles-capture-runner-temporarily`: After a graphic settles in a capture runner, temporarily override permanent `will-change` hints with `addStyleTag('*{will-change:auto !important}')`, wait two animation frames, remove the override, and wait two more frames before capturing.
- **trap** `wizard/follow-wizard-setup-flow-section-docs`: Do not follow the "The wizard is a SETUP flow" section of docs/SVG_IMPORT_PLAN.md. It describes the three-step walk from before the Text and Animation steps existed; the shipped order is the one this contract states.
- **trap** `wizard/hide-closed-author-rule-because-browser`: Hide a closed `<details>` with an author rule - `details:not([open]) > *:not(summary) { display: none }` - because the browser own `display: none` on non-summary children loses to ANY author `display`, and the Style step disclosures wrap a flex row. Assert measured HEIGHT is 0 in specs, never the `open` attribute.
- **trap** `wizard/keep-two-pro-package-rules-about`: Keep the two Pro package rules that are not about the door OUTSIDE the wizard step, and mutation-check them in the offline suite.
- **trap** `wizard/treat-entry-step-height-fixed-budget`: Treat the Entry step height as a fixed budget at 1366x768: the cards share one column, so growing one part is paid for out of another.
- **trap** `wizard/wait-layer-answer-surface-exist-driving`: Wait for a LAYER to answer through `awaitPickable`, not for the surface to exist, when driving the artwork canvas. A pointer is a ONE-SHOT and the rects arrive a frame after the document commits.
- **rule** `root/add-playwright-spec-any-new-flow`: Add a Playwright spec for any new UI flow, plus its mapping, in the same commit.
- **rule** `root/drive-freshness-time-never-commit-freshness`: Drive freshness by TIME, never by commit: the freshness check reports weekly and nothing auto-upgrades.
- **rule** `root/end-completed-waiting-turn-tiny-wrap`: End a completed or waiting turn with a tiny wrap-up somebody can read on a phone: what changed and whether it is verified, the exact action needed or "nothing", and the next step. Do the obvious safe continuation rather than asking permission for it. Put a question last on screen and add no prose after it, and run no extra scans just to produce the wrap-up.
- **rule** `root/keep-studio-open-there-login-wall`: Keep the studio open: there is no login wall, so create, preview, export and local saves work for everyone, hosted or self-hosted. Only account features gate themselves, and an offline build with no backend env grows ZERO auth UI.
- **rule** `root/let-pre-merge-gate-laptop-does`: Let CI be the pre-merge gate, not the laptop: it does strictly more, on a clean checkout. A clean `git merge main` is not proof the integration worked, because both sides were verified against a tree that no longer exists - after taking `main` in, run the integration plan from the FORK POINT so it covers both sides.
- **rule** `root/record-lesson-rule-goes-evidence-compiled`: Record a lesson with `npm run learn`: the rule goes to `contracts/rules/`, the evidence to `contracts/records/`, and the compiled files are never hand-edited. Do not add a paragraph to a contract instead - `check:contract-evidence` refuses one.
- **rule** `root/run-after-changes-keep-tree-lint`: Run `npm run build` after changes and keep the tree lint-clean rather than adding disable comments. There is no application unit-test suite, so never mark observable work done on a green build alone.
- **rule** `root/treat-only-section-push-everything-under`: Treat only the `NOW` section of `docs/GOALS.md` as the push; everything under `NEXT`, `THEN` and the parking lot is PARKED. Parked work is not started because a doc describes it well, unless that section carves out an exception in its own text.
- **rule** `root/treat-production-migrations-mechanism-permission-expect`: Treat production migrations as a MECHANISM, not a permission, and expect never to run one: a landing applies whatever production is missing once the branch is on `origin/main`. Only a REFUSAL reaches a person, answered per version and filed under `docs/acceptance/owner-queue/` by the branch own session; the landing succeeds either way.
- **rule** `root/treat-worktree-cleanup-mechanism-permission-worktree`: Treat worktree cleanup as a MECHANISM, not a permission: a worktree and its branch may go once every commit on the branch is an ancestor of a freshly fetched `origin/main` - not a clean tree, not "the session is finished". A worktree with NO branch is refused by its own rule. Classify ignored files before deleting: rebuildable output goes, a secret goes unread, and anything unrebuildable is archived outside the repo and verified file by file first.
- **rule** `root/work-feature-branch-own-worktree-made`: Work on a FEATURE BRANCH in its own worktree, made before the work starts, and commit each completed verified phase. Never add a `Co-Authored-By` trailer or any agent co-author, and do not commit `dist/` in feature work.
- **rule** `root/write-commit-message-outside-developer-reading`: Write a commit message an outside developer reading the history cold would understand, explaining the actual change. No chat or session language, no internal planning names, no AI-sounding phrases, and never mention agents, prompts or the conversation unless the commit is specifically about AI tooling.
- **rule** `wizard/keep-harness-default-renders-three-directions`: Keep the harness ON by default. On, it renders three directions as picker cards - a live MiniPreview of each built template plus its design words and a pass or fail mark. Off, it is one shot with static validation and no bench. Conversion of an imported template always runs the validated flow regardless of the checkbox.
- **rule** `wizard/keep-more-control-optional-structured-setup`: Keep "More control" OPTIONAL structured setup beside the prompt, editing ONE generation spec across category, data fields, look, fonts and animation. Collapsed sections show summary chips and keep their values, the spec persists as a cross-session draft and lands on the store at Create, and an EMPTY spec injects nothing so a prompt-only user never touches it.
- **rule** `wizard/lead-imported-design-animation-step-universal`: Lead the imported-design Animation step with the UNIVERSAL in and out bank in place of the category four whole-unit presets, which the bank stands in for. The pick lives in `draft.animation.motionIn` and `motionOut` and is written AT BUILD by `withUniversalMotion`, through the same engine the saved graphic control page applies afterwards. The default maps design-fade to fade.
- **rule** `wizard/show-page-browse-results-catalog-twelve`: Show a PAGE of Browse results, not the catalog: twelve plus a "Show 12 more", with both numbers stated in the count line. Keep `browseTemplates` returning the WHOLE result with no limit argument, spend the limit on the RANKING and then split it into the two sections, and derive the page reset during render off a signature rather than in an effect. In specs, search for a named design and assert `resultTotal`, never a card count.
- **taste** `root/keep-every-change-true-pillars-premium`: Keep every change true to the pillars: premium output with the least friction, so a non-technical user can make a great graphic AND run it live without touching code; client-agnostic with nothing mandatory; export anywhere from the one code-as-truth document, every target an adapter off it; and the code is real and always available, with the view optional and nothing hidden behind a visual-only scene model.
